title: VerusEval: Evaluating LLM-Generated Verus Specifications Beyond Verifier Acceptance
title_zh: VerusEval：超越验证器接受的LLM生成Verus规范评估

paragraphs.en: VerusEval框架提出六维度评估方法，发现验证器通过率高估LLM生成的Verus规范质量，语义正确率仅42.3%。 Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate Verus contracts for Rust programs together with the proofs that establish them. Yet verifier acceptance, the common measure of success, shows only that the implementation satisfies the generated contract, so it leaves open whether the contract captures the intended behavior. Assessing specification generation therefore requires an evaluation methodology, not a single metric. We present VerusEval, a framework that evaluates generated contracts along six dimensions, including Verus-native checks for semantic triviality, validated input-output (I/O) suites, and contract equivalence, and that relates them so that the strength and blind spots of each become measurable. Evaluating 13,716 artifacts from four workflows, five LLMs, and two prompting settings on 762 tasks, we find that acceptance overstates quality: only 42.3\% of the accepted artifacts complete all three semantic checks without a flag, and across workflows and models, higher acceptance does not consistently come with more correct contracts. I/O evaluation rejects 23.6\% of the accepted artifacts, yet only 63.2\% of those that pass it are proved equivalent. Of the accepted artifacts flagged by contract comparison, 84.1\% have a rejected completeness obligation, and the direction of a failure prioritizes inspection of the generated contract or the reference; it does not by itself establish which artifact is defective. Screening and review further identify 36 candidate defects among 61 selected reference contracts, and repairing one of them makes 10 of its 11 failing artifacts equivalent. Based on these findings, we derive four actionable lessons for evaluation, generation, and benchmark maintenance.
paragraphs.zh: VerusEval框架提出六维度评估方法，发现验证器通过率高估LLM生成的Verus规范质量，语义正确率仅42.3%。 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于为Rust程序生成Verus合约以及建立这些合约的证明。 然而验证器通过这一常用的成功衡量标准仅表明实现满足生成的合约，却无法回答合约是否捕捉了预期行为。 因此，评估规范生成需要一套评估方法学，而不是单一的指标。 我们提出VerusEval，这是一个沿六个维度评估生成合约的框架，包括针对语义平凡性的Verus原生检查、经过验证的输入输出（I/O）测试集以及合约等价性，并将这些维度相互关联，使每个维度的强度和盲点都变得可测量。 通过在762个任务上评估来自四种工作流、五个LLM和两种提示设置的13,716个工件，我们发现通过率高估了质量：在被接受的工件中，只有42.3%在没有标记的情况下完成全部三项语义检查，并且在不同工作流和模型中，更高的通过率并不总是伴随更正确的合约。 I/O评估拒绝了23.6%的被接受工件，而在通过该评估的工件中，只有63.2%被证明是等价的。 在被合约比较标记的被接受工件中，84.1%存在被拒绝的完备性义务，而失败的方向可优先指示应检查生成的合约还是参考合约；它本身并不能确定哪个工件有缺陷。 筛查和进一步审查在61个选定的参考合约中识别出36个候选缺陷，修复其中一个缺陷使该合约的11个失败工件中的10个变为等价。 基于这些发现，我们为评估、生成和基准维护总结出四条可操作的经验教训。
